# Freeze store integrity maintenance

Ensure the `TextFileBasedViolationStore` maintains the integrity of its `stored.rules` index and files.

Setting `default.integrity` to `repair` will check the index and folder as they are on disk during initialization, even if the same folder was initialized before. Defaulting to `ignore` which checks nothing.

If an entry points to a path that is not a regular file directly within the folder, it is broken. This also applies if the file name is not a valid path.

If an entry is not broken and its file has no violations it is resolved. Files that only contain line breaks are also resolved.

Entries that point to the same file name are shared, even if nothing exists with that name. If multiple entries point to the same regular file they are also shared. Including through a symbolic or hard link. Even if that file is outside the folder.

The `TextFileBasedViolationStore` will not touch any shared entries or files that no entry points to. If an entry is shared and anything else it will remain shared.

When set to `repair` broken entries will be discarded without touching whatever they point to.

When set to `repair` resolved entries and the file they point to will be discarded. If a resolved entry is a symbolic link the file it points to will be deleted as well.

If using `repair` and saving no violations for a known rule it will forget the rule. Its entry will be removed and its file as well. Unless another entry is sharing that file. In which case only the entry will be removed. Even if it points outside the folder. If using `repair` and saving no violations for an unknown rule nothing will be saved.

If it cannot delete the file of a rule it is forgetting it will fail to save and leave the entry.

Integrity maintenance has been implemented in [`TextFileBasedViolationStore`](file:///app/archunit/src/main/java/com/tngtech/archunit/library/freeze/TextFileBasedViolationStore.java).

### Summary of Changes

1. **Configuration Property**:
   - Added configuration property `default.integrity`, defaulting to `ignore` (which performs no integrity checks).
   - When set to `repair`, the store inspects the `stored.rules` index and directory as they exist on disk upon initialization (even if the store folder was initialized before).

2. **Integrity Verification & Repair on Initialization**:
   - **Broken entries**: An entry is considered broken if its target is not a regular file directly within the configured store directory, or if the file name is not a valid path. During repair, broken entries are discarded from `stored.rules` without touching whatever they point to.
   - **Resolved entries**: An unbroken entry whose file has no violations (including files containing only line breaks) is considered resolved. During repair, resolved entries are removed from `stored.rules` and their files are deleted. If the resolved entry points to a symbolic link, both the symbolic link and the file it points to are deleted.
   - **Shared entries**: Entries that point to the same file name (even if the file does not exist) or locate the same regular file (including via symbolic links or hard links, even outside the store folder) are identified as shared. Shared entries remain shared and are never touched or discarded during repair.
   - **Unreferenced files**: Files in the store directory not referenced by any index entry are left untouched.

3. **Rule Forgetting During Save**:
   - When saving no violations with `default.integrity=repair`:
     - **Unknown rules**: Nothing is saved; neither the index nor any files are created or modified.
     - **Known rules**: The store forgets the rule. If another entry shares the file (even if it points outside the store directory), only the rule entry is removed. Otherwise, both the entry and its file (including symbolic link targets) are deleted.
     - **Deletion failures**: If deleting the file fails, `save` fails with a `StoreUpdateFailedException` and leaves the entry in `stored.rules`.

4. **In-Memory Cache Synchronization**:
   - [`FileSyncedProperties`](file:///app/archunit/src/main/java/com/tngtech/archunit/library/freeze/TextFileBasedViolationStore.java#L438) now supports thread-safe reloading from disk (`reload()`), full property iteration (`getAllProperties()`), and key removals (`remove()`, `removeAll()`) that sync to the file system.

- Comprehensive unit tests covering all rules, symlinks, hard links, shared entries, outside-folder files, deletion failures, and `repair`/`ignore` modes were added to [`TextFileBasedViolationStoreTest`](file:///app/archunit/src/test/java/com/tngtech/archunit/library/freeze/TextFileBasedViolationStoreTest.java).
